Forms & validation

Source: vignettes/forms.Rmd
forms.Rmd

shadshiny inputs are ordinary Shiny inputs, so building and validating a form uses the reactivity you already know. This guide covers the field wrapper, the invalid state, server-side validation, and updating inputs.

Reading values

Every bound input contributes one reactive value under input$<inputId>. The shape matches the control: a string for text and select, a logical for checkbox and switch, a vector for multi-selects and toggle groups.

shad_input("email", label = "Email")
# server:
observe(print(input$email))     # the current string

The field wrapper

shad_form_field() gives any control a label, description, a required marker and an error slot — the standard anatomy of a form row. Wrap the input and pass the metadata to the wrapper:

shad_form_field(
  shad_input("site", placeholder = "example.com"),
  label = "Website",
  description = "No https:// needed.",
  required = TRUE
)

Many inputs also accept label / description directly for the common case, so reach for shad_form_field() when you need the error slot or a shared layout.

Signalling invalid input

Bound inputs take an invalid argument that switches them to the error style. Drive it from validation state and pair it with a message:

ui <- page_shad(
  shad_form_field(
    shad_input("email", label = "Email", type = "email"),
    inputId = "email",
    error = textOutput("email_err", inline = TRUE)
  ),
  shad_button("submit", "Sign up")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  valid_email <- reactive(grepl("^[^@ ]+@[^@ ]+\\.[^@ ]+$", input$email %||% ""))

  output$email_err <- renderText(
    if (!isTRUE(valid_email()) && nzchar(input$email %||% ""))
      "Enter a valid email address." else ""
  )

  observeEvent(input$submit, {
    if (!isTRUE(valid_email())) {
      shad_toast_error("Please fix the errors first.")
    } else {
      shad_toast_success(paste("Welcome,", input$email))
    }
  })
}

%||% (null-coalescing) is handy for guarding inputs before they’ve initialised: input$email %||% "". Define it once with `%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a)) b else a or import it from rlang.

The validator

Hand-rolling that per field gets old fast. shad_validator() does the same thing declaratively: you register rules per input, and it drives the field’s aria-invalid state and inline error text for you — no error = slot or textOutput() needed in the UI.

ui <- page_shad(
  shad_input("email", label = "Email", type = "email"),
  shad_input("pw", label = "Password", type = "password"),
  shad_button("submit", "Sign up")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  sv <- shad_validator()
  sv$add_rule("email", shad_rule_required())
  sv$add_rule("email", shad_rule_email())
  sv$add_rule("pw", shad_rule_min_chars(8))
  sv$enable()

  observeEvent(input$submit, {
    if (sv$validate()) shad_toast_success(paste("Welcome,", input$email))
  })
}

enable() starts live validation: errors appear as the user changes a field. validate() runs a full pass — it shows every error and returns a logical, which is what you want in a submit handler, since a field the user never touched has never been checked.

The rules

Rule Fails when
shad_rule_required(message) Value is empty, NULL, "", or an unchecked checkbox/switch.
shad_rule_email(message) Not a plausible email address.
shad_rule_min_chars(n, message) Shorter than n.
shad_rule_max_chars(n, message) Longer than n.
shad_rule_range(min, max, message) Not numeric, or outside [min, max].
shad_rule_regex(pattern, message) pattern doesn’t match.
shad_rule_in(choices, message) Any value is outside choices.
shad_rule_fn(fn) Your own function(value) returning an error string, or NULL to pass.

Every rule takes a message you can override. Rules for one field run in the order you added them and the first failure wins, so put shad_rule_required() first — every other rule passes an empty value on purpose, leaving “is this mandatory?” as a separate decision.

sv$add_rule("username", shad_rule_required())
sv$add_rule("username", shad_rule_regex("^[a-z0-9_]+$",
                                        "Lowercase, digits, and _ only."))
sv$add_rule("username", shad_rule_fn(function(value) {
  if (value %in% taken_usernames) "That username is taken." else NULL
}))

The rest of the object

Method Does
add_rule(inputId, rule, label) Register a rule. Chainable.
enable() / disable() Start / stop live validation (disable() clears the messages).
is_valid() Reactive logical: do all rules currently pass?
validate() Imperative full pass; shows every error, returns a logical.
fields() The registered input ids.
bind_submit(buttonId) Keep a shad_button() disabled while the form is invalid.
bind_summary(id) Render a shad_form_summary() of the outstanding errors. 
ui <- page_shad(
  shad_input("email", label = "Email", type = "email"),
  uiOutput("errors"),
  shad_button("submit", "Sign up")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  sv <- shad_validator()
  sv$add_rule("email", shad_rule_required(), label = "Email")
  sv$add_rule("email", shad_rule_email())
  sv$bind_submit("submit")     # button greys out until valid
  sv$bind_summary("errors")    # error list renders here on validate()
  sv$enable()
}

label = is the human name used in the summary; without it the summary falls back to the input id.

Standalone messages

The pieces the validator drives are also plain components, for when you want one without the machinery:

shad_form_message("We'll never share this.", type = "info")
shad_form_message("Username is taken.", type = "error")
shad_form_counter(nchar(input$bio %||% ""), 280)   # a 42/280 counter chip

Base validate() / need()

Still fine, and still the right tool for outputs — shad_validator() is about inputs. The two coexist.

Gating submission

Use shiny::req() to hold logic until required inputs are present and truthy, and validate the rest before acting:

observeEvent(input$submit, {
  req(input$email, input$plan)          # both must be truthy
  if (!isTRUE(input$tos)) {
    shad_toast_error("Please accept the terms.")
    return()
  }
  # ... persist the form ...
  shad_toast_success("Account created.")
})

Updating inputs from the server

Each valued component has an update_shad_*() twin. They take the same inputId, are Shiny-module safe, and are the way to reset or prefill a form:

observeEvent(input$reset, {
  updateTextInput(session, "email", value = "")   # shad_input uses the
  updateTextInput(session, "site", value = "")    # native text binding
  update_shad_select("plan", selected = "free")
  update_shad_checkbox("tos", value = FALSE)
  update_shad_slider("seats", value = 1)
})

Two things to note:

  • shad_input() and shad_textarea() render real <input>/<textarea> elements and use Shiny’s native text bindings. Update them with shiny::updateTextInput() / updateTextAreaInput(), not a update_shad_*() function (there isn’t one).
  • Everything else — select, combobox, checkbox, switch, radio, toggle(s), slider, OTP, calendar, date-picker — has a dedicated update_shad_*() helper. See the Server API guide for the full list.

A complete example 

library(shiny)
library(shadshiny)
`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a)) b else a

ui <- page_shad(
  theme_preset = "violet",
  shad_card(
    shad_card_header(shad_card_title("Create account")),
    shad_card_content(
      shad_input("email", label = "Email", type = "email",
                 placeholder = "you@example.com"),
      shad_input("pw", label = "Password", type = "password",
                 description = "At least 8 characters."),
      shad_select("plan", label = "Plan",
                  choices = c(Free = "free", Pro = "pro", Team = "team"),
                  selected = "pro"),
      shad_checkbox("tos", label = "I accept the terms")
    ),
    shad_card_footer(
      shad_button("submit", "Sign up"),
      shad_button("reset", "Reset", variant = "outline")
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  sv <- shad_validator()
  sv$add_rule("email", shad_rule_required(), label = "Email")
  sv$add_rule("email", shad_rule_email())
  sv$add_rule("pw", shad_rule_required(), label = "Password")
  sv$add_rule("pw", shad_rule_min_chars(8))
  sv$add_rule("tos", shad_rule_required("Accept the terms to continue."))
  sv$enable()

  observeEvent(input$reset, {
    updateTextInput(session, "email", value = "")
    updateTextInput(session, "pw", value = "")
    update_shad_select("plan", selected = "free")
    update_shad_checkbox("tos", value = FALSE)
  })

  observeEvent(input$submit, {
    if (sv$validate()) shad_toast_success(paste("Welcome,", input$email))
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
